props.gloss_en: on the fifth [Shabbat] one returns to the regular order
R' Ami: one returns to the order of the Torah portions
R' Yirmeya: one returns to the order of the haftarot
the mishna: for all [these] one interrupts [the order] -- New Moons, Chanukah, Purim, fasts, maamadot and Yom Kippur
the mishna's fast-day clause: on fasts one interrupts the order
Abaye's premise: there is a Torah portion on a weekday, but there is no haftara on a weekday -- so the mishna's weekday interruptions speak of the order of portions
Rav Huna: from the morning [of a fast], an assembly
Abaye: from morning to midday we examine the affairs of the town
Abaye: from midday to evening, a quarter of the day they read [the Torah] and the haftara, and a quarter of the day they pray
Abaye's verse: 'and they read in the book of the Torah of the Lord their God a quarter of the day, and a quarter they confessed and prostrated themselves' (Neh 9:3)

the stam: 'and to me gathered all who trembled at the words of the God of Israel over the exiles' trespass, and I sat appalled until the evening offering' (Ezra 9:4), and 'at the evening offering I rose from my fast' (Ezra 9:5)

supports.gloss_en: כוותיה דרבי אמי מסתברא, דתנן: לכל מפסיקין... -- the listed days include weekdays, and on a weekday there is a portion but no haftara (30b.4), so what is interrupted is the order of portions

deflected_by.gloss_en: ואידך: הא כדאיתא והא כדאיתא -- 'this as it is and that as it is' (Steinsaltz: on weekdays the mishna's interruption is of the portions, on Shabbat of the haftarot), so the mishna proves nothing

supports.gloss_en: מסייע ליה לרב הונא -- the mishna's interruption on fasts (rather than morning-regular, mincha-fast) fits Rav Huna: the morning is taken by the assembly

objections.gloss_en: ובתעניות למה לי הפסקה? ליקרי מצפרא בענינא דיומא, ובמנחה בתעניתא -- on fasts, why interrupt? read the day's regular matter in the morning and the fast portion at mincha

answered_by.gloss_en: מסייע ליה לרב הונא, דאמר רב הונא: מצפרא כינופיא -- the morning is given to the assembly, so there is no morning reading to keep (= p_rav_huna_kinufya)

objections.gloss_en: ואיפוך אנא? -- perhaps reverse it: read and pray in the first half, examine the town's affairs in the second

answered_by.gloss_en: לא סלקא דעתך, דכתיב: ...ואני יושב משומם עד למנחת הערב, וכתיב: ובמנחת הערב קמתי מתעניתי -- the gathering over the trespass came first, until the evening offering (= p_ezra_ad_minchat_haerev)
